issues.description: Method name inconsistency for the meal-cost calculation: the problem statement and UML specify a static method named calculateTotalPrice(Meal): int, but the template and solution artifacts use/mention a different name (computeMealCost). Specifically, the template Main calls shop.computeMealCost(...), the solution SealSaloon implements public static int computeMealCost(...), while the problem statement expects calculateTotalPrice and the solution's commented Main calls calculateTotalPrice. This mismatch in the expected method name will confuse students about which method to implement and may cause compilation/test failures if tests or instructions expect the other name.
issues.suggestedFix: Standardize the method name across all artifacts. Either (A) rename the method in the SealSaloon class to the problem-specified name calculateTotalPrice and update all template and solution references to call calculateTotalPrice(Meal), or (B) update the problem statement/UML to require computeMealCost(Meal). Ensure Main and any tests/documentation use the same name and that the method is static and returns int as specified.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a static method named calculateTotalPrice(Meal) on SealSaloon, but the provided implementation uses computeMealCost(Meal) as the static method name (and the template's commented Main also references computeMealCost). This naming divergence between the specification (calculateTotalPrice) and the implemented identifier (computeMealCost) creates a mapping barrier: students looking for calculateTotalPrice according to the exercise text will not find it in the codebase, and call sites (Main) and the implementation are inconsistently named across artifacts.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method name across all artifacts. Best fix: rename the static method computeMealCost(Meal) to calculateTotalPrice(Meal) in SealSaloon (public static int calculateTotalPrice(Meal meal)) and update all call sites (Main and template comments) accordingly. Alternatively, if computeMealCost is preferred, update the problem statement and UML to use computeMealCost consistently.
